summary: Actions on a thing, opened from a control.

pairs.dont: Use a dropdown menu to choose a value for a field.
pairs.do: Use Select for values; menus are for actions.
pairs.why: A menu does something when you pick a row. A select stores what you picked — different promises, different keyboard behaviour.

pairs.dont: Add a hover state to a menu row.
pairs.do: Leave focus to do the work.
pairs.why: Radix moves DOM focus on pointer-over as well as arrow keys, so one state covers both. A second one double-lights the row.

pairs.dont: Scatter destructive actions through the list.
pairs.do: Put them last, behind a separator.
pairs.why: The pointer travels down the list. A delete sitting mid-list is one slip away from the row above it.

pairs.dont: Show a shortcut the app has not bound.
pairs.do: Only show keys that actually work from that screen.
pairs.why: A printed shortcut is a promise. People try it once, and stop trusting the menu when it does nothing.

pairs.dont: Nest submenus more than one deep.
pairs.do: Flatten, or open a dialog for the complicated case.
pairs.why: Each level is another hover corridor to keep the pointer inside, and each one loses people.

a11y: Radix supplies the menu and menuitem roles, typeahead and arrow-key movement. Do not add roles of your own.
Disabled items use data-[disabled] rather than the disabled attribute — they keep pointer-events-none and 50% opacity but stay in the menu, so their existence is still discoverable.
Hover and keyboard focus are one state here, because Radix drives both through data-highlighted. There is no separate :focus-visible treatment to add.
The submenu chevron is aria-hidden; the item's text is its name.
CheckboxItem and RadioItem are deliberately not wrapped — use Radix's directly when a menu needs them, and they bring their own menuitemcheckbox and menuitemradio semantics.
